name: Root out inefficiencies
definition: Actively eliminate inefficiencies, simplify, and stay laser-focused on what really matters, whilst respecting any un-moveable constraints.

rows.under: Lives with the waste. Treats a slow process as just how things are.
rows.justRight: Actively finds and removes inefficiencies. Makes the next pass through the work cheaper than the last.
rows.over: Tears down a process that was carrying a real constraint. Creates a new mess in the name of speed.

rows.under: Adds steps. Leaves the complicated path in place because it already exists.
rows.justRight: Simplifies. Cuts the work that does not change the outcome.
rows.over: Simplifies past the point of safety. Drops the checks that were holding the product together.

rows.under: Treats every request as equal. The important work waits.
rows.justRight: Stays laser-focused on what really matters. Says no to work that does not move the outcome.
rows.over: Uses focus as a reason to ignore partners. "Not our priority" becomes a wall.

rows.under: Ignores a real constraint and plans as if it were optional. The plan fails on contact.
rows.justRight: Respects un-moveable constraints and designs around them. Does not waste energy fighting a wall that will not move.
rows.over: Treats every constraint as un-moveable. Stops looking for the ones that can actually change.

rows.under: Cuts nothing. The list only grows.
rows.justRight: Cuts the work that does not matter so the work that does can move. Explains the cut.
rows.over: Cuts the visible work and leaves the hidden waste. Looks efficient on a slide.
